primary_claim.location: Results: change in competitive fitness; Figure 2 and Table 2
primary_claim.finding: The primary study explicitly compares fitness change on live and heat-killed parasites after 16 generations and concludes that elevated host defence had no measurable cost.

official_data.location: COREE fitness data.xls, verified MD5 receipt
official_data.finding: The verified workbook contains background, treatment, generation, replicate, assay-pathogen, and in/out competition-count fields used for the reported cost test.

records.named_gap: A proposal to test whether defence evolution has a fitness cost in parasite-present versus parasite-absent conditions repeats the primary study's explicit design and reported comparison.

outcomes.positive: Reproducing no measurable cost would only repeat the published conclusion.
outcomes.null: A null or imprecise reanalysis would not supply a distinct scientific consequence.
outcomes.contrary: A changed estimate would require a new predeclared question and specialist review before challenging the published result.

primary_claim.finding: The primary report manipulated genotypic and stem-height trait diversity, collected non-destructive productivity measures over time, but reports its stated treatment model for the October 2012 endpoint with block as a random factor.

official_data.location: hughes_field_exp_repeated.csv header and verified MD5 receipt
official_data.finding: The verified repeated file contains Date, Block, Plot, genotypic diversity, trait diversity, treatment ID, and species-abundance fields.

records.named_gap: Whether the bounded diversity-by-performance interpretation is stable across the recorded repeated field observations, rather than being an endpoint-specific pattern, is not resolved by the stated October endpoint model.

outcomes.positive: A stable time-aware treatment pattern would strengthen only the bounded field-performance interpretation.
outcomes.null: A transient or imprecise pattern would restrict the claim to the reported endpoint.
outcomes.contrary: A time-dependent reversal would alter how the published interaction is interpreted across the experiment.

primary_claim.finding: The primary study compares young and old horses, tests multiple fascicles per tendon, and reports markedly fewer fatigue cycles to failure in aged fascicles.

official_data.location: README_for_Fatigue test raw data.txt and verified MD5 receipt
official_data.finding: The verified README identifies horse age, tendon type, fascicle number, test condition, and applied strain, preserving the nesting needed to audit the age comparison.

records.named_gap: Whether the reported age-associated fatigue difference remains under a horse-level rather than fascicle-level inferential unit is not resolved by the source receipt and requires direct inspection of the raw mechanical files and original analysis.

outcomes.positive: A horse-level result would support the bounded age-associated fatigue finding.
outcomes.null: Wider uncertainty would restrict confidence in the reported age contrast.
outcomes.contrary: A materially changed estimate would alter the interpretation of fascicle-level replication.

next_permitted_action: Retain the nematode rejection; complete closest-prior and raw-analysis audits for marsh and tendon records, and source a third V3-verified record rather than promoting either one.
